blocks.title: Etesian for the web.
blocks.lead: The design language is a set of web packages, so anything on the web can look and work like Etesian. This website and Cloud Companion’s web app are both built from them.

items.title: @etesian-design/tokens
items.text: The design tokens (colours, type, spacing, radii, motion) as CSS custom properties, TypeScript and JSON, and the open fonts used in place of the N9’s.

items.title: @etesian-design/vue
items.text: The Vue 3 components (HdButton, HdSwitch, HdToolBar, HdFastScroll and the rest), composables and the squircle geometry.

items.title: @etesian-design/quasar
items.text: A theme and integration for Quasar 2: brand colours, the icon set, the squircle spinner and the colour modes, so Quasar’s own components look Etesian.

items.title: @etesian-design/shell
items.text: The shell parts: the desktop (menu bar, dock, windows, Events, snapping, Overview), the mini apps and the Belle home-screen widgets.

blocks.heading: Installing the packages
blocks.intro: The packages are published to GitHub Packages. npm needs a GitHub token with read:packages in ~/.npmrc, even for public packages.
items: Install what you need: `npm install @etesian-design/vue @etesian-design/tokens`, and `@etesian-design/quasar` or `@etesian-design/shell` if you use them.
In a Quasar app, install the theme from a boot file: `app.use(EtesianQuasar, { mode: 'hybrid' })`.

blocks.heading: Quasar, themed
blocks.intro: Quasar is a Vue 3 framework. With the @etesian-design/quasar theme its own components (left) sit next to the library’s (right). Both columns are live.

blocks.heading: The Storybook
blocks.intro: Storybook is a workshop for UI components: each component, and whole screens built from them, rendered on their own with their measurements and notes. It is the visual reference for every component, built from the design repository and published with GitHub Pages at language.etesian-design.com. A few of its stories:

blocks.heading: How this site is built
paragraphs: This site is a Quasar (Vue 3) app, built as static pages (Quasar’s SSG mode) and published with GitHub Pages at etesian-design.com. It uses the four packages: the pages, the /try desktop and the phone are the library’s own components.

Each page is a JSON file of content blocks (text, features, pictures, live demos, release cards), checked when the site builds. Version numbers and dates are never typed into the text: they come from each project’s latest GitHub release, read when the site is built and again in your browser.

items.title: A browser in the cloud
items.text: Optional: Firefox runs on your server and its page is shown in the web app, or sent to phones too old for a modern web page.

items.title: A messaging gateway
items.text: SMS, Matrix, XMPP, IRC, Nextcloud Talk, Signal and Telegram, reachable from a SIP or XMPP phone or the web app.

items.title: Mail, calendar and contacts
items.text: In the web app, and through an optional hub that speaks Exchange ActiveSync, CalDAV and CardDAV for older phones.

items.title: Android in a browser tab
items.text: Optional: an Android system on your server, streamed to a web page with touch, keyboard, sound and clipboard.

paragraphs: Cloud Companion is a Phorepoc project, experimental, licensed AGPL-3.0. Its server is written in Go and runs with Docker; its web app is Vue 3 with Quasar, and imports the tokens, vue and shell packages with its own Quasar theme.

home.title: Etesian for the web.
home.lead: The design language is a Vue 3 component library, so anything on the web can look and work like Etesian.

home.title: This website
home.text: A working Etesian desktop and phone in the browser, built from the library’s own components: drag, snap and resize windows, open Events, swipe through the phone.

home.title: Cloud Companion
home.text: A Phorepoc project in the Etesian look: a small server you run yourself, with a browser, messaging, mail, calendar, contacts and Android in a browser tab.
